feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy-focused roles. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive, light on quantified outcomes beyond scale metrics, and has a few style/grammar inconsistencies.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions within one organization strongly support leadership growth and trust.  
- Strong strategic/technical blend: combines digital strategy, CMS/platform work, analytics, governance, and multimedia in a way that feels senior and marketable.  
- Good clarity and structure: headline, summary, competencies, experience, and technical skills are easy to scan and relevant to target roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more impact metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more outcome-focused results would strengthen impact (e.g., engagement growth, conversion gains, efficiency improvements, cost savings).  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap significantly; consolidating would improve focus and save space.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: add “of” in “more than 12 years of experience”; standardize serial commas (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “content operations and enterprise web improvement”); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, currently learning).” No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it’s slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it with sharper phrasing and one or two concrete differentiators will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Lead with your strongest value proposition: digital strategy leadership for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a tighter grouping like “multi-channel digital communications.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience building and leading multi-channel programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in web and CMS modernization, cross-channel content operations, and the workflows, governance, and analytics systems that support complex teams. Strong background in advocacy communications, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” closely repeat Core Competencies.
- “Advocacy messaging” and “stakeholder coordination” also reappear in Topline Skills and Soft Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and making terms more distinct will improve scan value.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, resume-style nouns/phrases and tighten wording: “Multi-channel communications,” “Web platform & CMS administration,” “Analytics, reporting & optimization.”
- Replace vague or overlapping items like “Workflow & systems architecture” with clearer, more CV-friendly language such as “Content operations & workflow design” or “Digital systems & governance.”
- Prioritize the most marketable, recent strengths from experience: digital strategy, CMS/platform modernization, analytics, governance, advocacy communications, multimedia production.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications • Web platform & CMS administration • Content operations & editorial workflow design • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Digital systems & governance • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with “Topline Skills”; consider using this section for broader leadership themes and leaving tools/platforms to later sections.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also repeats Soft Skills almost verbatim.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good strategic/technical range, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo entries. Tighten it around what is new in the consultant scope, especially AI search, platform improvement, and cross-channel governance.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + level: “Advise a national membership organization on digital strategy, platform modernization, and content operations for enterprise web and communications programs.”
- Combine overlapping duties into 3–4 sharper bullets; e.g., “Redesigned digital workflows, analytics, and governance to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia teams.”
- Make the Drupal/CMS bullet outcome-oriented: mention number of sites, users, toolkits launched, publishing efficiency gains, or reduced support burden if available.
- Elevate the most distinctive work: “Lead AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content model, and discovery UX to improve member access to resources.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics…” repeats themes already covered in Director/Associate roles.
- “Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation…” may duplicate skills sections unless tied to a specific project/result.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management language already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the website bullets and foreground impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight more outcome-focused: replace “Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels…” with specifics such as audience growth, engagement, campaign performance, or newsletter/social results if available.
- Tighten remaining bullets: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast-quality video studio…” / “Expanded analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Email, social media, and video” leadership overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- “Governance/publishing workflows” also appears in the current consultant role; use distinct wording or sharper outcomes here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like support work than a step-up role. Tighten it to emphasize ownership, cross-functional leadership, and channel growth without repeating website/video points covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope and leadership: “Led day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social media, and advocacy content, improving coordination among communications, policy, and program teams.”
- Combine newsletter bullets and add scale/results if available: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders, improving consistency, timeliness, and audience engagement.”
- Reframe video bullet around launch/growth: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace “helped improve” with stronger ownership: “Built more consistent editorial planning and digital publishing workflows, streamlining cross-team content production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Website/platform governance overlaps with Director of Digital Media; keep this role focused on operations and editorial coordination.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the channel.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, less repetitive language:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance, workflow design & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “audience-focused content planning” for “content operations” or “workflow design,” which better reflects your recent leadership work.
- Use “cross-channel” instead of “multi-channel” for consistency with the header and stronger executive tone.
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve measurable outcomes for experience bullets, not skills sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “public-sector and advocacy messaging” repeat ideas already stated in the header.
- “Editorial systems and governance” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Editorial workflow design” and “Workflow & systems architecture.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant mix of platforms and execution skills, but this item is too broad and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to current work rather than listing every tool.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool dump to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Put Drupal first and de-emphasize older/lower-priority platforms unless they are job-relevant; consider dropping either SharePoint or Power Pages if space is tight.
- Replace “AI-enabled search experiences” with “AI-enabled search and content discovery” for clearer business value.
- If possible, add one qualifier elsewhere in the CV to support this section, e.g., “Drupal migration for 10,000+ pages” or “enterprise web properties serving 3.5M annual page views.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave full tool inventory to that section.
- “CMS modernization” also overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Web & CMS administration.”

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design

- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack for your most recent leadership roles, but it reads as a generic keyword list. Tighten it around decision-making impact and avoid repeating “reporting/analytics” language already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language, e.g. “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace weaker phrases with sharper ones: “KPI framework development” instead of “KPI design”; “executive dashboarding” instead of “leadership reporting”
- Add optimization language tied to business use: “web performance and SEO analysis” or “behavioral insights and conversion optimization”
- Suggested version: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio & Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework development • Executive dashboarding • Behavioral insights, SEO & web performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Data analytics & reporting” already appears in Core Competencies; this skills line should stay tool- and outcome-focused, not repeat that wording.
- Power BI, Looker Studio, BigQuery, GA4, and Clarity are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so keep this section concise rather than restating impact claims.

items.title: University of Virginia

Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” This section should either add level/scope context or be tightened to avoid repeating the same CMS names elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “CMS & Web Publishing Platforms” for clearer positioning.
- Add proficiency/scope cues tied to recent work, e.g.: “Drupal (enterprise migration, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, prioritize strongest/recent platform first and de-emphasize lighter-use tools: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint; working knowledge of Power Pages and GitHub Pages”
- Keep punctuation consistent and avoid listing platforms already explained in depth elsewhere unless this section is meant as a quick-scan skills index.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” Topline Skills entry almost exactly; consider merging or using this section for only tools not named there.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent NACo roles, so repeating it without context adds little.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools most relevant to recent Drupal/platform modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Front-End & Technical Implementation”
- Replace with a tighter list: “HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions”
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the rest of the CV uses similarly specific technical notation.
- If accurate, add one outcome-oriented qualifier in parentheses, e.g. “API integrations (CMS, analytics, campaign tools)” or “GitHub Actions (deployment/workflow automation).”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears under Topline Skills; keep the stronger phrasing in one place only.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may make GitHub Actions feel repetitive unless framed specifically as deployment/CI tooling.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful tool coverage, but this item is currently just a software list and overlaps with stronger “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” language elsewhere. Make it tighter and more capability-led so it supports recent systems work without repeating it.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Group by function for clarity: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier • Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp • Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to use: “for workflow automation, project coordination, and cross-team communication”
- Consider trimming weaker/older tools if not used recently; keep the most relevant to current consulting/director work first (Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, Teams)

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are similar category tools; listing all four can read as keyword stacking unless all are genuinely current.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this item should emphasize systems/platform fluency rather than repeat channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and standardize platform naming: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in brief parenthetical form to show practical use: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys (campaign automation) • Higher Logic (member/community communications) • Mailchimp (newsletter deployment)**
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, place it first to reflect recency and depth.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters,” “audience engagement,” or campaign management language here; that is already covered in recent Work Experience.
- If Higher Logic was not meaningfully used, remove it rather than listing a weaker platform just to fill space.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story and scope, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize foundational impact, promotion, and distinct early-career contributions.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground advancement and team-building: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Make the website/video work more concrete: specify platform refresh, livestreamed events, weekly video series, or volume/frequency if known.
- Replace soft phrasing like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows” with outcomes: improved publishing speed, expanded in-house production, increased content cadence, or reduced reliance on vendors.
- Suggested version: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations. Contributed to a major website refresh, produced livestreams and a recurring weekly video update, and helped formalize cross-channel publishing workflows. Provided day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching or initially producing the series.
- “Strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia” is repeated throughout later NACo entries; keep this version more foundational.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory, but it reads broadly and undersells impact. Since later NACo roles already cover digital leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation/research support plus the podcast launch.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the strongest differentiator: “Supported county innovation and policy initiatives through research, project coordination, and digital content development.”
- Make the podcast achievement the second sentence and tighten phrasing: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add scope or outcome: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or how content advanced member engagement/program visibility.
- Consider a concise final version: “Coordinated research and innovation projects supporting NACo programs and policy priorities, while developing digital and multimedia content. Launched the organization’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid overemphasizing general digital content production; later roles already cover web/video/multimedia growth in more depth.
- Don’t repeat “first”/foundational team-building language already used in the 2015–2018 and 2022–2024 entries.
